e: South Korea recalls its ambassador to Ukraine, citing the latter's decision to reveal the transfer of North Korean POWs the previous month.
President Zelenskyy announces that two North Korean soldiers that had been captured in Ukraine while fighting for Russia had been transferred to South Korea.
The US approves a $2.68 billion sale of air defense equipment to Ukraine, to be financed using a combination of European contributions and US foreign military financing.
Russia holds legislative elections in occupied areas of Ukraine that it seized in 2022 for the first time.
Ruslan Kravchenko resigns as Prosecutor General amid allegations of money-laundering involving call centers engaged in financial scams.
A shootout between units of the SBU and HUR in Kyiv injures three HUR agents.
The Verkhovna Rada approves the appointment of Yevhenii Khmara as defense minister.
Ukraine repatriates the remains of nationalist leader Yevhen Konovalets from the Netherlands for an official reburial in Kyiv.
A Russian soldier carries out a mass shooting in Khmelnytske, Crimea, killing four people including another soldier before being arrested.
A Chabad center in Hadiach is damaged by fire, causing millions of dollars in losses.
President Zelenskyy dismisses Oleksandr Syrskyi as Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, replacing him with Mykhailo Drapatyi amidst protests demanding Syrskyi’s removal.
President Zelenskyy appoints Serhii Koretskyi as prime minister.
Dismissal of Mykhailo Fedorov: President Zelenskyy dismisses defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov, sparking nationwide protests.
Yulia Svyrydenko resigns as prime minister as part of a cabinet reshuffle by president Zelenskyy.

Polish president Karol Nawrocki strips president Zelenskyy of the Order of the White Eagle, Poland's highest state honour, after Zelenskyy honored a special operations forces unit with the name "Heroes of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army", a Nazi-collaborating organization that conducted massacres against Poles in Volhynia and Eastern Galicia.
Bulgaria announces that it would stop supplying weapons to Ukraine.
Former Supreme Court president Vsevolod Kniaziev is sentenced to five years' imprisonment following a plea-bargain agreement for bribery.
One person is killed in an explosion at a sorting depot of Nova Poshta in Obolonskyi District, Kyiv.
A Russian air attack destroys the Ukrainian National Chernobyl Museum in Kyiv and damages the National Art Museum of Ukraine.
A suspected Ukrainian drone is shot down by a Romanian fighter jet belonging to a NATO contingent over central Estonia, prompting an apology from Ukraine.
Ukraine repatriates the remains of nationalist leader Andriy Melnyk and his wife Sofia from Luxembourg for an official reburial in Kyiv, which is held on 25 May.
A law simplifying the legalization of foreign personnel serving in the Armed Forces of Ukraine and the National Guard comes into effect.
Ukraine's Viktoria Leléka finishes ninth at Eurovision 2026 in Austria with the single "Ridnym".
Thirty-six countries and the European Union join the Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression against Ukraine.
The European Union approves a €90 billion loan package for Ukraine.
Six people, including the gunman, are killed in a mass shooting and hostage crisis at a supermarket in Kyiv.
Ihor Polishchuk resigns as mayor of Lutsk amid a corruption investigation against him.
Archbishop Nykodym of Sumy and Okhtyrka (formerly Volodymyr Kobzar) is elected as head of the Ukrainian Orthodox Church – Kyiv Patriarchate following the death of Filaret Denysenko on 20 March.
Former MP Lyudmila Marchenko is sentenced to two years' imprisonment by the High Anti-Corruption Court of Ukraine for bribery.

Ukraine boycotts the closing ceremony of the 2026 Winter Paralympics in Italy in protest over Russian athletes being allowed to compete under the Russian flag after the lifting of sanctions imposed over the Russian invasion in 2022.
Ukraine and Romania sign a strategic partnership agreement in the defense and energy sectors.
President Zelenskyy confirms the deployment of interceptor drones and specialists to help protect U.S. military bases in Jordan amid the 2026 Iran war.
The European Commission rebukes President Zelenskyy over remarks that Hungary interpreted as a threat against Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán.

Ukraine boycotts the opening ceremony of the 2026 Winter Paralympics in Italy in protest over Russian athletes being allowed to compete under the Russian flag after the lifting of sanctions imposed over the Russian invasion in 2022.
President Zelenskyy says he would prefer not to repair the Druzhba oil pipeline.

Ukraine accuses Hungary of hostage-taking and theft following the detention of two vans and seven staff of the Ukrainian bank Oschadbank by Hungarian authorities while transiting cash through to Austria.
A suspect in the 2025 murder of politician Andriy Portnov is arrested in Heinsberg, Germany.
Slovakia halts exports of emergency electricity supplies to Ukraine, citing attacks on the Druzhba pipeline.
Hungary and Slovakia suspend exports of diesel fuel to Ukraine, citing attacks on the Druzhba pipeline.
Former energy minister German Galushchenko is arrested while attempting to flee Ukraine aboard a train amid corruption charges against him.
